primitives.name: URL Path Segment Classifier
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'P': 'path segment identifier (dimensionless)', 'S(P)': 'service status of path P (binary: 0/1)'}
primitives.assumptions: Each path segment maps to a discrete service state; paths are mutually exclusive and collectively exhaustive.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When S(P) = 0, path is inaccessible or non-operational.

layer2.mapping: URL path space is isomorphic to a finite-state automaton where each segment represents a node and S(P) defines edge validity.
layer2.telemetry: Crawl success rate per path segment

primitives.name: Service Availability Detector
primitives.verbatim_quote: | |---|---| | `https://tipico.com/` | Tipico No Service | | `https://tipico.com/years/` | Tipico No Service |
primitives.assumptions: Availability is deterministic over time intervals; service status is static during observation window.
primitives.breakdown_regime: A = 0 when service returns error or timeout.

layer2.mapping: Derived from path classifier via temporal sampling of HTTP response codes; kernel maps path → availability vector.
layer2.telemetry: HTTP status code frequency per path

primitives.name: Crawlability Indexer
primitives.verbatim_quote: # tipico.com — crawl URLs reached: **10** ## Path segments | Segment | URLs | |---|---|
primitives.assumptions: All crawled URLs are equally valid for indexing; crawlability is independent of content depth.
primitives.breakdown_regime: C < 1 when URL set is incomplete or blocked.

layer2.mapping: Crawlability is isomorphic to a graph connectivity measure; U defines node cardinality in crawl graph.

Failure modes emerge when paths are unreachable due to blocking or misconfiguration, leading to zero availability. These primitives support a layered inference model where path semantics inform service logic, and service data informs crawl strategy.
